data.name: InfoQueryDaxDefineColumnDesc
data.value: The DEFINE COLUMN statement lets you define a calculated column local to a query. The column is not persisted in the model, it exists only for the lifetime of the query. Apart from that, it is a calculated column in every sense of the term.

data.name: InfoQueryDaxDefineMeasuresDesc
data.value: The MEASURE keyword introduces a measure definition (DEFINE) in a query (also known as query measure). <br/> The syntax after MEASURE defines a measure, which can be consumed in any other expression of the same query.<br/> A query measure overrides a model measure with the same name for the duration of the query. They will not affect the model measure.

data.name: InfoQueryDaxDefineTableDesc
data.value: The DEFINE TABLE statement lets you define a calculated table local to a query. </br>The table is not persisted in the model, it exists only for the lifetime of the query. </br>Apart from that, it is a calculated table in every sense of the term albeit with some limitations.

data.name: InfoQueryDaxDefineVarDesc
data.value: The VAR keyword introduces variables in an expression.<br/>The syntax after VAR defines a variable, which can be consumed in following VAR statements or within the mandatory RETURN statement following the declaration of one or more variables.<br/><br/>If VAR is used in the DEFINE section of an EVALUATE statement, it can be used in any expression of the statement and the RETURN keyword cannot be used.

data.name: InfoQueryDaxEvaluateDesc
data.value: EVALUATE is a DAX statement that is needed to execute a query. </br></br> EVALUATE followed by any table expression returns the result of the table expression. </br>Moreover, one or more EVALUATE statements can be preceded by special definitions like local tables, columns, measures, and variables that have the scope of the entire batch of EVALUATE statements executed together. <br/><br/>An EVALUATE statement is divided into three parts: <br/><b> - DEFINE - Definition section: </b> it includes the definition of local entities like tables, columns, variables, and measures. <br/> - <b>EVALUATE - Query expression: </b> it contains the table expression to evaluate and return as the result.<br/> - <b> Result modifiers: </b> an optional additional section to EVALUATE, which is introduced by the keyword ORDER BY. It includes the sort order of the result and the optional definition of which rows to return, by providing a starting point with START AT.<br/><br/> The first and third parts of the statement are optional. Thus, one can just use EVALUATE followed by any table expression to produce a query.

data.name: InfoQueryDaxSelectColumnsDesc
data.value: Allows you to choose which columns to take given a table. In turn, it allows you to alias columns or add new columns through DAX expressions.

data.name: InfoQueryDaxSelectColumnsParamExpression
data.value: (Optional) (Repeatable) The expression for the new column to be added.

data.name: InfoQueryDaxSelectColumnsParamName
data.value: (Optional) The name of the new column to be added.

data.name: InfoQueryDaxSelectColumnsParamTable
data.value: The table from which columns are selected.

data.name: InfoQueryDaxSelectColumnsReturnValues
data.value: (TABLE) - Return a table with the same number of rows as the table specified as the first argument.

data.name: InfoQueryDaxTopNDescription
data.value: Returns a given number of top rows according to a specified expression.
